In the past, a supercomputer was precisely that, a single very expensive machine.

However, once computers became widely available, it became much more affordable to connect a lot of standard hardware and distribute the tasks you want to run across the entire system.

Thus, a modern supercomputer consists of nodes, each of which is similar to a typical high-end server. Any specialized hardware that differs from an average server is found in the technology the nodes use to communicate with each other, known as the interconnect, rather than in the CPU, memory, or storage.

What makes a supercomputer fast is the number of nodes and the code designed to run in parallel, rather than any individual node being particularly exceptional.

On turbo trainers, the easiest way to maintain power is to determine the speed that corresponds to a specific power output and then hold that speed. This results in a consistent power line.

I find this approach much simpler than trying to rely on 1, 3, 10, or 30-second power averages directly.

Additionally, power is not the only important metric. There are some long descents where I actually use speed to assess my improvement (such as braking less and taking corners faster).

Finally, for time trial and hill climb competitions, I use speed to estimate how long the effort will take, then adjust my power output accordingly. Admittedly, GPS speed is accurate enough for this purpose.

EDIT: Just so you know, I wouldn't upgrade my cycling computer for these reasons alone. Nor would I use the less reliable speed sensor, but the newer wheel-hub sensors are quite effective for this type of use.

The following things, in my opinion, negatively affect someone's quality of life:

* Not being able to think straight in the morning until having had one or many cups of coffee,
* Withdrawal effects (as you've mentioned, when you can't get coffee),
* The cyclic effect it can have on your sleep patterns (drink coffee, stay up late, need more coffee to get you started the next day),

A few things I do to cut down the amount of coffee that I drink and reduce the negative effects it has:

* Don't drink coffee past midday; not only does this mean you'll drink less, but it also means that your brain will be used to functioning without it. Finally, you are also drinking it when it's going to help you the most and reducing the effects that it'll have on your sleep.
